name: Test
summary: Test is reserved for errors that only apply while in self-test mode.

name: BlankPkgName
summary: BlankPkgName occurs when a package name is the blank identifier "_".

name: MismatchedPkgName
summary: MismatchedPkgName occurs when a file's package name doesn't match the package name already established by other files.

name: InvalidPkgUse
summary: InvalidPkgUse occurs when a package identifier is used outside of a selector expression.

name: BadImportPath
summary: BadImportPath occurs when an import path is not valid.

name: BrokenImport
summary: BrokenImport occurs when importing a package fails.

name: ImportCRenamed
summary: ImportCRenamed occurs when the special import "C" is renamed. "C" is a pseudo-package, and must not be renamed.

name: UnusedImport
summary: UnusedImport occurs when an import is unused.

name: InvalidInitCycle
summary: InvalidInitCycle occurs when an invalid cycle is detected within the initialization graph.
examples:
var x int = f()

func f() int { return x }

name: DuplicateDecl
summary: DuplicateDecl occurs when an identifier is declared multiple times.

name: InvalidDeclCycle
summary: InvalidDeclCycle occurs when a declaration cycle is not valid.

name: InvalidTypeCycle
summary: TODO(markfreeman): Retire InvalidTypeCycle, as it's never emitted.

name: InvalidConstInit
summary: InvalidConstInit occurs when a const declaration has a non-constant initializer.

name: InvalidConstVal
summary: InvalidConstVal occurs when a const value cannot be converted to its target type.

name: InvalidConstType
summary: InvalidConstType occurs when the underlying type in a const declaration is not a valid constant type.

name: UntypedNilUse
summary: UntypedNilUse occurs when the predeclared (untyped) value nil is used to initialize a variable declared without an explicit type.

name: WrongAssignCount
summary: WrongAssignCount occurs when the number of values on the right-hand side of an assignment or initialization expression does not match the number of variables on the left-hand side.

name: UnassignableOperand
summary: UnassignableOperand occurs when the left-hand side of an assignment is not assignable.

name: NoNewVar
summary: NoNewVar occurs when a short variable declaration (':=') does not declare new variables.

name: MultiValAssignOp
summary: MultiValAssignOp occurs when an assignment operation (+=, *=, etc) does not have single-valued left-hand or right-hand side.

name: InvalidIfaceAssign
summary: InvalidIfaceAssign occurs when a value of type T is used as an interface, but T does not implement a method of the expected interface.

name: InvalidChanAssign
summary: InvalidChanAssign occurs when a chan assignment is invalid.
examples:
type T1 chan int
type T2 chan int

var x T1
// Invalid assignment because both types are named
var _ T2 = x

name: IncompatibleAssign
summary: IncompatibleAssign occurs when the type of the right-hand side expression in an assignment cannot be assigned to the type of the variable being assigned.

name: UnaddressableFieldAssign
summary: UnaddressableFieldAssign occurs when trying to assign to a struct field in a map value.

name: NotAType
summary: NotAType occurs when the identifier used as the underlying type in a type declaration or the right-hand side of a type alias does not denote a type.

name: InvalidArrayLen
summary: InvalidArrayLen occurs when an array length is not a constant value.

name: BlankIfaceMethod
summary: BlankIfaceMethod occurs when a method name is '_'.

name: IncomparableMapKey
summary: IncomparableMapKey occurs when a map key type does not support the == and != operators.

name: InvalidPtrEmbed
summary: InvalidPtrEmbed occurs when an embedded field is of the pointer form *T, and T itself is itself a pointer, an unsafe.Pointer, or an interface.

name: BadRecv
summary: BadRecv occurs when a method declaration does not have exactly one receiver parameter.

name: InvalidRecv
summary: InvalidRecv occurs when a receiver type expression is not of the form T or *T, or T is a pointer type.

name: DuplicateFieldAndMethod
summary: DuplicateFieldAndMethod occurs when an identifier appears as both a field and method name.

name: DuplicateMethod
summary: DuplicateMethod occurs when two methods on the same receiver type have the same name.

name: InvalidBlank
summary: InvalidBlank occurs when a blank identifier is used as a value or type.

name: InvalidIota
summary: InvalidIota occurs when the predeclared identifier iota is used outside of a constant declaration.

name: MissingInitBody
summary: MissingInitBody occurs when an init function is missing its body.

name: InvalidInitSig
summary: InvalidInitSig occurs when an init function declares parameters or results.

name: InvalidInitDecl
summary: InvalidInitDecl occurs when init is declared as anything other than a function.

name: InvalidMainDecl
summary: InvalidMainDecl occurs when main is declared as anything other than a function, in a main package.

name: TooManyValues
summary: TooManyValues occurs when a function returns too many values for the expression context in which it is used.

name: NotAnExpr
summary: NotAnExpr occurs when a type expression is used where a value expression is expected.

name: TruncatedFloat
summary: TruncatedFloat occurs when a float constant is truncated to an integer value.

name: NumericOverflow
summary: NumericOverflow occurs when a numeric constant overflows its target type.

name: UndefinedOp
summary: UndefinedOp occurs when an operator is not defined for the type(s) used in an operation.

name: MismatchedTypes
summary: MismatchedTypes occurs when operand types are incompatible in a binary operation.
examples:
var a = "hello"
var b = 1
var c = a - b

name: DivByZero
summary: DivByZero occurs when a division operation is provable at compile time to be a division by zero.

name: NonNumericIncDec
summary: NonNumericIncDec occurs when an increment or decrement operator is applied to a non-numeric value.

name: UnaddressableOperand
summary: UnaddressableOperand occurs when the & operator is applied to an unaddressable expression.

name: InvalidIndirection
summary: InvalidIndirection occurs when a non-pointer value is indirected via the '*' operator.

name: NonIndexableOperand
summary: NonIndexableOperand occurs when an index operation is applied to a value that cannot be indexed.

name: InvalidIndex
summary: InvalidIndex occurs when an index argument is not of integer type, negative, or out-of-bounds.

name: SwappedSliceIndices
summary: SwappedSliceIndices occurs when constant indices in a slice expression are decreasing in value.

name: NonSliceableOperand
summary: NonSliceableOperand occurs when a slice operation is applied to a value whose type is not sliceable, or is unaddressable.

name: InvalidSliceExpr
summary: InvalidSliceExpr occurs when a three-index slice expression (a[x:y:z]) is applied to a string.

name: InvalidShiftCount
summary: InvalidShiftCount occurs when the right-hand side of a shift operation is either non-integer, negative, or too large.

name: InvalidShiftOperand
summary: InvalidShiftOperand occurs when the shifted operand is not an integer.

name: InvalidReceive
summary: InvalidReceive occurs when there is a channel receive from a value that is either not a channel, or is a send-only channel.

name: InvalidSend
summary: InvalidSend occurs when there is a channel send to a value that is not a channel, or is a receive-only channel.

name: DuplicateLitKey
summary: DuplicateLitKey occurs when an index is duplicated in a slice, array, or map literal.

name: MissingLitKey
summary: MissingLitKey occurs when a map literal is missing a key expression.

name: InvalidLitIndex
summary: InvalidLitIndex occurs when the key in a key-value element of a slice or array literal is not an integer constant.

name: OversizeArrayLit
summary: OversizeArrayLit occurs when an array literal exceeds its length.

name: MixedStructLit
summary: MixedStructLit occurs when a struct literal contains a mix of positional and named elements.

name: InvalidStructLit
summary: InvalidStructLit occurs when a positional struct literal has an incorrect number of values.

name: MissingLitField
summary: MissingLitField occurs when a struct literal refers to a field that does not exist on the struct type.

name: DuplicateLitField
summary: DuplicateLitField occurs when a struct literal contains duplicated fields.

name: UnexportedLitField
summary: UnexportedLitField occurs when a positional struct literal implicitly assigns an unexported field of an imported type.

name: InvalidLitField
summary: InvalidLitField occurs when a field name is not a valid identifier.

name: UntypedLit
summary: UntypedLit occurs when a composite literal omits a required type identifier.

name: InvalidLit
summary: InvalidLit occurs when a composite literal expression does not match its type.

name: AmbiguousSelector
summary: AmbiguousSelector occurs when a selector is ambiguous.

name: UndeclaredImportedName
summary: UndeclaredImportedName occurs when a package-qualified identifier is undeclared by the imported package.

name: UnexportedName
summary: UnexportedName occurs when a selector refers to an unexported identifier of an imported package.

name: UndeclaredName
summary: UndeclaredName occurs when an identifier is not declared in the current scope.

name: MissingFieldOrMethod
summary: MissingFieldOrMethod occurs when a selector references a field or method that does not exist.
examples:
type T struct {}

var x = T{}.f

name: BadDotDotDotSyntax
summary: BadDotDotDotSyntax occurs when a "..." occurs in a context where it is not valid.

name: NonVariadicDotDotDot
summary: NonVariadicDotDotDot occurs when a "..." is used on the final argument to a non-variadic function.

name: InvalidDotDotDot
summary: InvalidDotDotDot occurs when a "..." is used in a non-variadic built-in function.

name: UncalledBuiltin
summary: UncalledBuiltin occurs when a built-in function is used as a function-valued expression, instead of being called.

name: InvalidAppend
summary: InvalidAppend occurs when append is called with a first argument that is not a slice.

name: InvalidCap
summary: InvalidCap occurs when an argument to the cap built-in function is not of supported type.

name: InvalidClose
summary: InvalidClose occurs when close(...) is called with an argument that is not of channel type, or that is a receive-only channel.

name: InvalidCopy
summary: InvalidCopy occurs when the arguments are not of slice type or do not have compatible type.

name: InvalidComplex
summary: InvalidComplex occurs when the complex built-in function is called with arguments with incompatible types.

name: InvalidDelete
summary: InvalidDelete occurs when the delete built-in function is called with a first argument that is not a map.

name: InvalidImag
summary: InvalidImag occurs when the imag built-in function is called with an argument that does not have complex type.

name: InvalidLen
summary: InvalidLen occurs when an argument to the len built-in function is not of supported type.

name: SwappedMakeArgs
summary: SwappedMakeArgs occurs when make is called with three arguments, and its length argument is larger than its capacity argument.

name: InvalidMake
summary: InvalidMake occurs when make is called with an unsupported type argument.

name: InvalidReal
summary: InvalidReal occurs when the real built-in function is called with an argument that does not have complex type.

name: InvalidAssert
summary: InvalidAssert occurs when a type assertion is applied to a value that is not of interface type.

name: ImpossibleAssert
summary: ImpossibleAssert occurs for a type assertion x.(T) when the value x of interface cannot have dynamic type T, due to a missing or mismatching method on T.

name: InvalidConversion
summary: InvalidConversion occurs when the argument type cannot be converted to the target.

name: InvalidUntypedConversion
summary: InvalidUntypedConversion occurs when there is no valid implicit conversion from an untyped value satisfying the type constraints of the context in which it is used.

name: BadOffsetofSyntax
summary: BadOffsetofSyntax occurs when unsafe.Offsetof is called with an argument that is not a selector expression.

name: InvalidOffsetof
summary: InvalidOffsetof occurs when unsafe.Offsetof is called with a method selector, rather than a field selector, or when the field is embedded via a pointer.

name: UnusedExpr
summary: UnusedExpr occurs when a side-effect free expression is used as a statement. Such a statement has no effect.

name: UnusedVar
summary: UnusedVar occurs when a variable is declared but unused.

name: MissingReturn
summary: MissingReturn occurs when a function with results is missing a return statement.

name: WrongResultCount
summary: WrongResultCount occurs when a return statement returns an incorrect number of values.

name: OutOfScopeResult
summary: OutOfScopeResult occurs when the name of a value implicitly returned by an empty return statement is shadowed in a nested scope.

name: InvalidCond
summary: InvalidCond occurs when an if condition is not a boolean expression.

name: InvalidPostDecl
summary: InvalidPostDecl occurs when there is a declaration in a for-loop post statement.

name: InvalidIterVar
summary: InvalidIterVar occurs when two iteration variables are used while ranging over a channel.

name: InvalidRangeExpr
summary: InvalidRangeExpr occurs when the type of a range expression is not a valid type for use with a range loop.

name: MisplacedBreak
summary: MisplacedBreak occurs when a break statement is not within a for, switch, or select statement of the innermost function definition.

name: MisplacedContinue
summary: MisplacedContinue occurs when a continue statement is not within a for loop of the innermost function definition.

name: MisplacedFallthrough
summary: MisplacedFallthrough occurs when a fallthrough statement is not within an expression switch.

name: DuplicateCase
summary: DuplicateCase occurs when a type or expression switch has duplicate cases.

name: DuplicateDefault
summary: DuplicateDefault occurs when a type or expression switch has multiple default clauses.

name: BadTypeKeyword
summary: BadTypeKeyword occurs when a .(type) expression is used anywhere other than a type switch.

name: InvalidTypeSwitch
summary: InvalidTypeSwitch occurs when .(type) is used on an expression that is not of interface type.

name: InvalidExprSwitch
summary: InvalidExprSwitch occurs when a switch expression is not comparable.

name: InvalidSelectCase
summary: InvalidSelectCase occurs when a select case is not a channel send or receive.

name: UndeclaredLabel
summary: UndeclaredLabel occurs when an undeclared label is jumped to.

name: DuplicateLabel
summary: DuplicateLabel occurs when a label is declared more than once.

name: MisplacedLabel
summary: MisplacedLabel occurs when a break or continue label is not on a for, switch, or select statement.

name: UnusedLabel
summary: UnusedLabel occurs when a label is declared and not used.

name: JumpOverDecl
summary: JumpOverDecl occurs when a label jumps over a variable declaration.
examples:
func f() int {
	goto L
	x := 2
L:
	x++
	return x
}

name: JumpIntoBlock
summary: JumpIntoBlock occurs when a forward jump goes to a label inside a nested block.

name: InvalidMethodExpr
summary: InvalidMethodExpr occurs when a pointer method is called but the argument is not addressable.

name: WrongArgCount
summary: WrongArgCount occurs when too few or too many arguments are passed by a function call.
examples:
func f(i int) {}
var x = f()

name: InvalidCall
summary: InvalidCall occurs when an expression is called that is not of function type.

name: UnusedResults
summary: UnusedResults occurs when a restricted expression-only built-in function is suspended via go or defer. Such a suspension discards the results of these side-effect free built-in functions, and therefore is ineffectual.

name: InvalidDefer
summary: InvalidDefer occurs when a deferred expression is not a function call, for example if the expression is a type conversion.

name: InvalidGo
summary: InvalidGo occurs when a go expression is not a function call, for example if the expression is a type conversion.

name: BadDecl
summary: All codes below were added in Go 1.17.

name: RepeatedDecl
summary: RepeatedDecl occurs when an identifier occurs more than once on the left hand side of a short variable declaration.

name: InvalidUnsafeAdd
summary: InvalidUnsafeAdd occurs when unsafe.Add is called with a length argument that is not of integer type. It also occurs if it is used in a package compiled for a language version before go1.17.

name: InvalidUnsafeSlice
summary: InvalidUnsafeSlice occurs when unsafe.Slice is called with a pointer argument that is not of pointer type or a length argument that is not of integer type, negative, or out of bounds. It also occurs if it is used in a package compiled for a language version before go1.17.

name: UnsupportedFeature
summary: All codes below were added in Go 1.18.

name: NotAGenericType
summary: NotAGenericType occurs when a non-generic type is used where a generic type is expected: in type or function instantiation.

name: WrongTypeArgCount
summary: WrongTypeArgCount occurs when a type or function is instantiated with an incorrect number of type arguments, including when a generic type or function is used without instantiation.
examples:
type T[p any] int

var _ T[int, string]

func f[T any]() {}

var x = f

name: CannotInferTypeArgs
summary: CannotInferTypeArgs occurs when type or function type argument inference fails to infer all type arguments.

name: InvalidInstanceCycle
summary: InvalidInstanceCycle occurs when an invalid cycle is detected within the instantiation graph.

name: InvalidUnion
summary: InvalidUnion occurs when an embedded union or approximation element is not valid.

name: MisplacedConstraintIface
summary: MisplacedConstraintIface occurs when a constraint-type interface is used outside of constraint position.

name: InvalidMethodTypeParams
summary: InvalidMethodTypeParams occurs when methods have type parameters.

name: MisplacedTypeParam
summary: MisplacedTypeParam occurs when a type parameter is used in a place where it is not permitted.

name: InvalidUnsafeSliceData
summary: InvalidUnsafeSliceData occurs when unsafe.SliceData is called with an argument that is not of slice type. It also occurs if it is used in a package compiled for a language version before go1.20.

name: InvalidUnsafeString
summary: InvalidUnsafeString occurs when unsafe.String is called with a length argument that is not of integer type, negative, or out of bounds. It also occurs if it is used in a package compiled for a language version before go1.20.

name: InvalidClear
summary: InvalidClear occurs when clear is called with an argument that is not of map or slice type.

name: TypeTooLarge
summary: TypeTooLarge occurs if unsafe.Sizeof or unsafe.Offsetof is called with an expression whose type is too large.
examples:
import "unsafe"

type E [1 << 31 - 1]int
var a [1 << 31]E
var _ = unsafe.Sizeof(a)

name: InvalidMinMaxOperand
summary: InvalidMinMaxOperand occurs if min or max is called with an operand that cannot be ordered because it does not support the < operator.
examples:
var s, t []byte
var _ = max(s, t)

name: TooNew
summary: TooNew indicates that, through build tags or a go.mod file, a source file requires a version of Go that is newer than the logic of the type checker. As a consequence, the type checker may produce spurious errors or fail to report real errors. The solution is to rebuild the application with a newer Go release.
